key_insight: ESI-Bench reframes perception as an active process by making the observer an actor: agents must move and interact to reveal occluded spatial properties (structure, dynamics, containment, functionality), closing the perception–action loop.
problem_solved: Prior spatial-intelligence benchmarks assume oracle or passive observations and cannot evaluate how actions change what can be perceived; ESI-Bench provides tasks and metrics that test an agent's ability to actively gather observations and reason about unseen, occluded, or functional aspects of environments.
method: Introduce ESI-Bench: a simulated embodied benchmark suite with tasks specifically designed to require active exploration and interaction to infer occluded spatial information.
Define evaluation protocols and metrics that measure the closed-loop perception–action performance (e.g., information gain, task success after active sensing, efficiency of sensing actions).
Provide baseline agent implementations and analyses to highlight common failure modes and quantify gaps between passive/oracle and active embodied approaches.
impact: ESI-Bench enables development and rigorous evaluation of agents that plan sensing actions as part of perception, accelerating progress toward robots and models that robustly infer 3D structure and function in realistic, occluded settings.

paper_title: ESI-Bench: Towards Embodied Spatial Intelligence that Closes the Perception-Action Loop
paper_authors: Yining Hong, Jiageng Liu, Han Yin, Manling Li, Leonidas Guibas
